Draft Effective date: effective date

Pantry is a recipe book and meal planner for households. This policy says what Pantry collects about you, why, who can see it, and what you can do about it. We have tried to write it so you can read it in a few minutes.

Who runs Pantry

Pantry is made by Darren Sill Technical Services Ltd, a one-person company registered in Ireland (company number 789126). In this policy "we" and "us" mean that company.

For anything about your data, email support@thepantryapp.ie. We are the "controller" of your data under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

The short version

  • We collect what you need to use Pantry: your sign-in details, your name and photo if you add them, and the recipes, plans, lists and notes you put in the app.
  • Everything you add to a pantry is shared with the other members of that pantry.
  • A recipe you mark Public can be seen by everyone who uses Pantry.
  • There are no ads. We do not sell your data. Pantry has no analytics or tracking tools.
  • You can delete your account in the app. Some things you added to a shared pantry stay with that household afterwards. See "When you delete your account".

What we collect and why

Your account

  • Email address and password, if you sign up with email. Your password is stored only as a scrambled hash. We use your email to sign you in and to send account emails, such as a password reset code.
  • Sign in with Apple, if you use it. Apple tells us your email address (or a private relay address, if you choose "Hide My Email") and, the first time only, your name. We use the name as your display name if you have not set one.
  • Display name and profile photo, if you add them. Other people see these next to the things you do (see "Who can see your data").
  • Unit preference (metric or imperial). The app picks a starting value from your phone's region setting. The region itself is not sent to us.
  • Technical sign-in records. When you sign in, our hosting provider records the session, the time, and the device's IP address, to keep you signed in and to protect accounts.

What you put in the app

  • Pantries (households): the name of each pantry, who is in it, each member's role (owner or member), and invite codes.
  • Recipes: titles, descriptions, ingredients, steps, times, tags, the web address you imported from, and recipe photos.
  • Meal plans and planned meals, including who planned or swapped a meal.
  • Shopping lists and items, including who added and who ticked off an item.
  • Staples (the household's stock list), including who added each one.
  • Collections of recipes, and likes.
  • The cook log: when a recipe was cooked, by whom, and any note or star rating you add.
  • Reports and blocks: if you report a recipe or a person, we keep the report, the reason you picked and any details you write. If you block someone, we keep that.
  • Failed invite codes: when someone enters an invite code that does not work, we note the attempt for about an hour, to stop people guessing codes.

Things that stay on your phone

  • Your sign-in session is kept in the phone's secure storage (the iOS Keychain on iPhone).
  • Some settings, a draft meal plan you have not saved, and running cook timers are kept in the app's own storage on the phone.
  • Scan a Page reads the text from a photo on your phone, using Apple's built-in text recognition. The photo is not sent to us. Paste Text is also read on the phone.
  • Cook timers use notifications scheduled on your phone. We do not send push notifications and do not collect a push notification token.

Camera and photos

Pantry asks to use your camera or photo library only when you choose to add a photo to a recipe, set a profile photo, or scan a recipe page. A recipe photo is resized and saved as a new image before it is uploaded. You can turn these permissions off in your phone's settings at any time.

What we do not collect

We do not collect your location, contacts, health data, or payment details. We do not use advertising or analytics tools, and we do not track you across other apps or websites.

Why we may use your data (lawful basis)

GDPR requires a legal reason for each use of your data. Ours are:

What we do Legal reason
Create and run your account, sign you in, send account emails Contract: we need it to provide the app you asked for
Store your recipes, plans, lists, staples, collections, likes and cook log Contract
Share what you add with the other members of your pantry Contract: sharing with your household is what the app does
Show Public recipes to all Pantry users Contract: you choose to make a recipe Public
Import a recipe from a web address you give us Contract
Handle reports, hide harmful content, block users, limit invite-code guessing Legitimate interests: keeping Pantry safe for its users
Keep technical logs and backups Legitimate interests: keeping the service secure and working
Answer your privacy requests, and keep records the law requires Legal obligation

Where we rely on legitimate interests, you can object (see "Your rights").

Who can see your data

Other members of your pantry

Everything in a pantry belongs to the whole household. Every member of a pantry can see:

  • your display name and profile photo;
  • every recipe, collection, meal plan, shopping list and staple in that pantry, and who added, planned, swapped or ticked off each one;
  • the cook log, including who cooked what, when, and any notes and ratings;
  • which recipes members have liked, and who liked them.

Members can also edit the pantry's recipes. Only join a pantry with people you trust with this information.

Everyone who uses Pantry

  • Public recipes. When you mark a recipe Public, every signed-in Pantry user can find it on Explore, along with your display name and profile photo.
  • Your profile. Your display name and profile photo can be seen by any signed-in Pantry user, even if you never publish a recipe. Do not use a name or photo you want to keep private.
  • Photos are stored at public web addresses. Recipe photos and profile photos are stored at web addresses that anyone who has the address can open, without signing in. A recipe photo's address contains a long random code, so it cannot be guessed, but anyone you share it with, or anyone in your pantry, could pass it on.

People with an invite code

Anyone who has your pantry's invite code can see the pantry's name before joining, and can join it until the code expires (7 days) or is changed.

Us

We can see all data in Pantry's database when we need to: to fix a problem, to act on a report, or to answer your request. We review reported content by hand. We do not read your data for any other reason.

Service providers (processors)

We use these companies to run Pantry. They handle data only on our instructions.

  • Supabase (Supabase's legal entity) hosts Pantry's database, sign-in, photo storage and server functions. All the data above, except what stays on your phone, is stored with Supabase in Supabase project region.
  • Apple provides Sign in with Apple, if you use it, and distributes the app through the App Store and TestFlight. Apple's own privacy policy covers what Apple collects.
  • Email delivery: account emails, such as password reset codes, are sent by email sender: Supabase's built-in email, or the custom SMTP provider's name.

Websites you import from

When you import a recipe by web address, our server fetches that page for you. The website sees a request from our server, not from your phone. If our server cannot be reached, the app may fetch the page directly from your phone, and then the website sees your phone's IP address.

An imported recipe can keep the original website's photo. That photo is loaded from the original website each time someone views the recipe, so that website can see the viewer's IP address, as with any web image.

We do not sell your data, share it with advertisers, or give it to anyone else unless the law requires it.

Where your data is stored

Your data is stored by Supabase in Supabase project region. Supabase is a US company, so some data may be reached from outside the EU, for example when Supabase gives technical support. the transfer safeguard, see PR notes Apple may process sign-in data outside the EU under its own safeguards.

How long we keep your data

  • Your account and what you add: for as long as you have an account. When you delete your account, see the next section.
  • Things you delete in the app (a recipe, a list item, a planned meal) are removed from the live database straight away. Meal plans are not deleted: a finished plan is archived and stays in the pantry's history.
  • Recipe photos and profile photos are not yet deleted automatically when you delete your account or a pantry. We will delete them on request; email us. change this line once photo clean-up exists
  • Failed invite-code attempts: about one hour.
  • Reports: until we have dealt with them, and then how long resolved reports are kept. A report you made is deleted when you delete your account.
  • Backups: Supabase keeps backups of the database for backup retention for the plan in use. Deleted data may stay in a backup until that backup expires.
  • Technical logs (sign-ins, server requests, IP addresses) are kept for Supabase log retention for the plan in use.

When you delete your account

You can delete your account in the app: Settings → Delete account. You must confirm with your password, or with Apple if you use Sign in with Apple. Here is what happens.

Deleted straight away:

  • your account, email address, display name and unit preference;
  • any pantry you own where you are the only member, and everything in it;
  • recipes you created outside any pantry;
  • your likes, your blocks, and reports you made;
  • your membership of every pantry.

Kept by the household. Things you added to a pantry shared with other people belong to that household, so they stay after you leave:

  • Recipes you added to someone else's pantry pass to that pantry's owner.
  • Meal plans, planned meals, shopping lists, collections, staples, ticked-off items and the cook log stay in the pantry. They no longer show your name: they show no author.
  • Your cook log notes and ratings stay in the household's cook log, without your name. Any remaining member can then edit or delete them. If you want them gone, delete them before you delete your account.

Before you can delete your account: if you own a pantry that other people still use, you must first hand it to another member or delete it. This stops a household losing its data.

Copies others have made: if you made a recipe Public and another person liked it, deleting the recipe (or your account) leaves that person with a private copy of it.

Not yet deleted automatically: your profile photo and recipe photos stay at their web addresses until we remove them. Email us and we will. remove this paragraph once account deletion removes photos

Your rights

Under GDPR you have the right to:

  • access the data we hold about you, and get a copy;
  • correct data that is wrong (you can change most of it yourself in the app);
  • delete your data (you can delete your account in the app);
  • take your data with you in a common format (the app can export your recipes; for anything else, email us);
  • object to us using your data where we rely on legitimate interests;
  • restrict how we use your data while a complaint is being looked at.

To use any of these rights, email support@thepantryapp.ie. We will reply within one month. We may ask you to confirm the request comes from your account's email address.

You can also complain to the Irish Data Protection Commission (www.dataprotection.ie). We would like the chance to fix the problem first, so please contact us too.

Children

Pantry is not meant for children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect data from them. If you think a child under 16 has an account, email us and we will delete it. confirm the minimum age of 16

Security

Your data travels between the app and our servers over encrypted connections. Your sign-in session is kept in your phone's secure storage. Database rules decide who can read each record, so you see only your own pantries and Public recipes. Passwords are stored only as hashes. Pantry is made by a one-person company, not a security team, and no system is perfectly secure. If we learn of a breach that puts your data at risk, we will tell you and the Data Protection Commission as the law requires.

Changes to this policy

If we change this policy, we will update the date at the top. If a change matters, for example a new use of your data or a new service provider, we will tell you in the app or by email before it takes effect.
